# TAMARYS

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Research federation of the CNRS (FRA 2018), formerly GDR TAMARYS |
| **Country** | France, with European and industrial partners |
| **Coordination** | Benoît Rousseau (CNRS, [LTeN Nantes](/network/lten-cnrs.html)) |
| **Scope** | Thermal radiation–matter interaction (UV to IR) · materials for extreme environments · high-temperature systems and multiphysics simulation |
| **Applications** | Decarbonising high-temperature industrial processes · reusable thermal protection for aerospace |
| **Training** | [RTSTM 2026 thematic school](/events-news/schools/2026-rtstm-hendaye.html), Hendaye, 3–9 October 2026 |
| **Official site** | [tamarys.cnrs.fr](https://tamarys.cnrs.fr/) |

## Why it matters for emissivity

TAMARYS gathers French expertise in heat transfer, materials for extreme
environments and reactive flows. Radiation–matter interaction is one of its
three priorities, and that is where emissivity sits: the property that
connects a material's structure to the radiation it emits at high temperature.
It also brings together academic laboratories and an Industrial Partner Club,
the combination that decides whether radiative-property data reaches
engineering practice.
